title: An RDMA-First Object Storage System with SmartNIC Offload (ROS2)
event_hint: Proposes ROS2, an RDMA-first object storage design that offloads the DAOS client onto an NVIDIA BlueField-3 SmartNIC to remove host mediation from the AI I/O data path.
problem: AI training and inference impose sustained, fine-grain I/O that stresses host-mediated, TCP-based storage paths; host mediation in the data path becomes a bottleneck for GPU-centric pipelines.
mechanism: ROS2 offloads the DAOS client to an NVIDIA BlueField-3 SmartNIC while leaving the DAOS I/O engine unchanged on the storage server. It splits a lightweight gRPC control plane (namespace and capability exchange) from a high-throughput UCX/libfabric data plane (RDMA or TCP), removing host mediation from the data path.

evidence.claim: On server-grade CPUs, RDMA consistently outperforms TCP for both large sequential and small random I/O.
evidence.condition: FIO/DFS across local and remote configurations on server-grade CPUs

evidence.claim: When the DAOS client runs on BlueField-3, end-to-end performance is comparable to running it on the host, preserving RDMA efficiency after offload.
evidence.baseline: DAOS client on the host CPU
evidence.condition: DAOS client offloaded to NVIDIA BlueField-3 SmartNIC over RDMA

evidence.claim: TCP on the SmartNIC lags host performance, underscoring the importance of RDMA for offloaded deployments.
evidence.condition: DAOS client on BlueField-3 over TCP

evaluation_context: Evaluated with FIO/DFS across local and remote configurations, comparing RDMA vs. TCP data planes and DAOS-client-on-host vs. DAOS-client-on-BlueField-3. Storage server keeps the DAOS I/O engine unchanged.
limitations: Abstract-level only; full body not fetched. The abstract reports qualitative ordering (RDMA > TCP; SmartNIC-RDMA comparable to host; SmartNIC-TCP below host) but no specific throughput/IOPS numbers or magnitudes; exact figures require the full PDF.
project_relevance: Directly relevant to DPU/SmartNIC offload: it demonstrates offloading a real object-storage client (DAOS) to BlueField-3 while keeping RDMA line-rate benefit, a concrete pattern for removing host mediation from AI-training/inference storage I/O. The control-plane/data-plane split and UCX/libfabric RDMA datapath align with SmartNIC-offload architecture interests.
